To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miR-19 members of the miR-92/17 cluster can regulate BRCA2 expression in a cell type-specific manner and that miR-92a, miR-17, miR-20a, and miR-92b do not affect BRCA2 expression.

the miR-92a-19a-19b-92b-20a-20b cluster of six miRNAs has the ability to post-transcriptionally regulate BRCA2 expression in a cell line dependent manner, and that the miR19a/b:BRCA2 interactions are direct and involve a MRE in the BRCA 3′UT.
miR-19 regulates BRCA2 expression and that the effect of miR-19 on BRCA2 depends on the cellular context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes, which have been linked to the etiology of breast cancer.
the post-transcriptionally regulated expression of BRCA2, which is a major component in the DNA damage response and repair pathway.
identifying the molecular mechanisms by which miRNAs contribute to the development of BRCAness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the miR-92/17 cluster has a complex effect on BRCA2 expression and the mechanism of this effect is cell type dependent.
miR-19 is an important post-transcriptional regulator of BRCA2 in a subset of cancer cell lines.
miR-19 and BRCA2 are involved in a post-transcriptional feedback loop that is cell-type dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRCA2’s post-transcriptional expression is subject to complex regulation that may contribute to the development of cancers with a ‘BRCAnes’ phenotype.
miR-19 regulates BRCA2 expression in a cell type specific manner.
miRNAs may play an important role in the regulation of the expression of the BRCA2 protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
post-transcriptional mechanisms may be involved in the development of BRCAness in cancers.
the miR-92a/19a/19b/20/92b cluster may contribute to the BRCAness phenotype through the regulation of BRCA1 and BRCA2 expression.
miR-17-92 cluster members have the potential to regulate the abundance of BRCAA2 mRNA and protein in a cell type-specific manner, which has implications in the development of cancers with BRCAness.
